- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.30) or is flat (0.00), model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; adjust downward only if sentiment remains negative.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in subsequent periods; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean-reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 3–5 day moving average to dampen volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores trend reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment decay, not price momentum.
